jp: 友達[ともだち]{から|kara-source}電話[でんわ]{が|ga-subject}ありました。
en: I got a call from a friend.
why: The caller is where the call comes from, so the sender is marked with から, not a location or object particle.

jp: 母[はは]{から|kara-source}手紙[てがみ]{が|ga-subject}届[とど]きました。
en: A letter arrived from my mother.
why: With a thing that arrives, the sender is the source and takes から; に would make your mother the recipient.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{から|kara-source}メール{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました。
en: An email came from my teacher.
why: The sender of something that comes to you is marked with から; に would turn the teacher into the receiver.

jp: 兄[あに]{から/に|kara-source}カメラ{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed a camera from my older brother.
why: The person you borrow from is the source of the camera and is marked with から (に also works with 借りる).

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{から|kara-source}連絡[れんらく]{が|ga-subject}ありました。
en: There was a message from the company.
why: The company is where the contact originated, so it is marked as the source with から.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{から/に|kara-source}いい話[はなし]{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: I heard a good story from my teacher.
why: The person you hear something from is its source, marked with から (に also works with 聞く).

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{から/に|kara-source}昔[むかし]{の|no-possessive}話[はなし]{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: I heard stories of the old days from my grandmother.
why: The person who tells you a story is its source and takes から (に is also possible with 聞く).

jp: このニュース{は|wa-topic}田中[たなか]さん{から/に|kara-source}聞[き]きました。
en: I heard this news from Mr. Tanaka.
why: Mr. Tanaka is who the news came from, so he is marked with から (に also works with 聞く).

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}人[ひと]{から/に|kara-source}傘[かさ]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed an umbrella from the person next door.
why: The lender is the source of the umbrella and takes から (に also works with 借りる).

jp: 誕生日[たんじょうび]{に|ni-time}父[ちち]{から/に|kara-source}時計[とけい]{を|o-object}もらいました。
en: I got a watch from my father on my birthday.
why: With もらう, the giver is the source and is marked with から (に also works).

jp: 姉[あね]{から/に|kara-source}もらったセーター{は/が|wa-topic}とても暖[あたた]かいです。
en: The sweater I got from my sister is very warm.
why: The person you received the sweater from is its source, marked with から (に also works with もらう).

jp: 外国[がいこく]{の|no-possessive}友達[ともだち]{から|kara-source}カード{が|ga-subject}届[とど]きました。
en: A card arrived from a friend abroad.
why: The sender of something that arrives is the source and takes から; に would make the friend the receiver.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{から|kara-source}メール{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました{か|ka-question}。
en: Did an email come from Ms. Yamada?
why: The sender of an incoming email is marked with から; に would mean the email came to Ms. Yamada.

jp: 市役所[しやくしょ]{から|kara-source}大切[たいせつ]な書類[しょるい]{が|ga-subject}届[とど]きました。
en: An important document arrived from the city office.
why: The office that sent the document is its source, so it takes から; に would make the office the receiver.

jp: 病院[びょういん]{から|kara-source}電話[でんわ]{が|ga-subject}かかってきました。
en: I got a phone call from the hospital.
why: With 電話がかかってくる, the caller is marked with から; に would make the hospital the one receiving the call.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、林[はやし]さん{から/に|kara-source}プレゼント{を|o-object}もらいました。
en: Yesterday I got a present from Ms. Hayashi.
why: The giver of the present is its source and is marked with から (に also works with もらう).

jp: 友達[ともだち]{から/に|kara-source}借[か]りた本[ほん]{を|o-object}もう読[よ]みました。
en: I have already read the book I borrowed from a friend.
why: Inside the modifying clause, the lender is still the source of the book and takes から (に also works).

jp: 母[はは]{から/に|kara-source}料理[りょうり]{を|o-object}習[なら]いました。
en: I learned cooking from my mother.
why: The person who teaches you is the source of the skill, marked with から (に also works with 習う).

jp: 友達[ともだち]{から/に|kara-source}旅行[りょこう]{の|no-possessive}お土産[みやげ]{を|o-object}もらいました。
en: I got a travel souvenir from a friend.
why: The giver of the souvenir is the source and is marked with から (に also works with もらう).

jp: 兄[あに]{から|kara-source}来[き]た手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}読[よ]みました。
en: I read the letter that came from my older brother.
why: The sender of something that comes to you is marked with から; に would mean the letter came to your brother.

jp: その情報[じょうほう]{は|wa-topic}どこ{から|kara-source}来[き]たんですか。
en: Where did that information come from?
why: Asking about the origin of information, the source is marked with から; どこに would ask where it went.

jp: 親[おや]{から/に|kara-source}お金[かね]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed money from my parents.
why: Your parents are the lender, i.e. the source of the money, so they take から (に also works with 借りる).

jp: 知[し]らない人[ひと]{から|kara-source}メール{が|ga-subject}来[き]{て|te-sequence}、びっくりしました。
en: An email came from a stranger and I was surprised.
why: The sender of an incoming email is marked with から; に would mean the email was sent to the stranger.

jp: 大学[だいがく]{から|kara-source}合格[ごうかく]{の|no-possessive}通知[つうち]{が|ga-subject}届[とど]きました。
en: A notice of acceptance arrived from the university.
why: The university that sent the notice is its source and takes から; に would make it the receiver.

jp: 山本[やまもと]さん{から/に|kara-source}新[あたら]しい仕事[しごと]{の|no-possessive}話[はなし]{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: I heard about a new job from Mr. Yamamoto.
why: Mr. Yamamoto is who the information came from, marked with から (に also works with 聞く).

jp: 弟[おとうと]{から/に|kara-source}ゲーム{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed a game from my younger brother.
why: The lender is the source of the game and takes から (に also works with 借りる).

jp: だれ{から/に|kara-source}この花[はな]{を|o-object}もらったんですか。
en: Who did you get these flowers from?
why: Asking for the giver, the person you received something from is marked with から (に also works).

jp: 参加者[さんかしゃ]{から|kara-source}たくさん質問[しつもん]{が|ga-subject}出[で]ました。
en: Lots of questions came from the participants.
why: The people the questions came from are their source, so they take から; に would make them the ones being asked.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{から/に|kara-source}レポート{の|no-possessive}書[か]き方[かた]{を|o-object}教[おし]えてもらいました。
en: My teacher taught me how to write a report.
why: The person who teaches is the source of the knowledge, marked with から (に also works with もらう).

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}先輩[せんぱい]{から/に|kara-source}ギター{を|o-object}もらいました。
en: I got a guitar from a senior colleague at work.
why: The senior colleague is the giver, so he or she is the source of the guitar and takes から (に also works).

jp: お客[きゃく]さん{から|kara-source}注文[ちゅうもん]{の|no-possessive}電話[でんわ]{が|ga-subject}ありました。
en: A customer called in with an order.
why: The customer is the origin of the call, so the source takes から; に would make the customer the receiver.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}大豆[だいず]{から/で|kara-source}豆腐[とうふ]{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: My mother makes tofu from soybeans.
why: The raw material that is transformed into something else takes から: soybeans become tofu (で is also used here).

jp: ワイン{は|wa-topic}ぶどう{から|kara-source}作[つく]られます。
en: Wine is made from grapes.
why: The raw material that becomes the product is marked with から; に would make the grapes the agent.

jp: バター{は|wa-topic}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{から|kara-source}作[つく]ります。
en: Butter is made from milk.
why: Milk is the raw material that is changed into butter, which is what から marks.

jp: チョコレート{は|wa-topic}何[なに]{から|kara-source}作[つく]られるか知[し]っていますか。
en: Do you know what chocolate is made from?
why: Asking about the raw material that is processed into a product, the material takes から.

jp: このせっけん{は|wa-topic}オリーブ{の|no-possessive}実[み]{から|kara-source}作[つく]られています。
en: This soap is made from olive fruit.
why: The ingredient that is processed into the soap is marked with から.

jp: しょうゆ{は|wa-topic}大豆[だいず]{と|to-and}小麦[こむぎ]{から|kara-source}作[つく]られます。
en: Soy sauce is made from soybeans and wheat.
why: The ingredients that are processed into the product take から, here after the pair 大豆と小麦.

jp: この言葉[ことば]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{から|kara-source}来[き]ています。
en: This word comes from English.
why: The language a word originates from is its source and takes から.

jp: このトイレットペーパー{は|wa-topic}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]パック{から|kara-source}作[つく]られています。
en: This toilet paper is made from milk cartons.
why: The cartons are pulped and turned into something new, so the raw material takes から.

jp: この会社[かいしゃ]{は|wa-topic}古[ふる]いペットボトル{から|kara-source}服[ふく]{を|o-object}作[つく]っています。
en: This company makes clothes from old plastic bottles.
why: Bottles are the raw material turned into clothes, so they take から.

jp: 牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{から|kara-source}チーズ{が|ga-subject}できます。
en: Cheese is made from milk.
why: The raw material from which a product comes into being takes から; できる states what comes out of it.

jp: 日本酒[にほんしゅ]{は|wa-topic}米[こめ]{から|kara-source}作[つく]られます。
en: Sake is made from rice.
why: Rice is the raw material that is turned into sake, which is what から marks.
